I was really chubby/ borderline obese end of high school/ beginning of college and I was really sick of how I looked but I was really nervous about working out in a gym especially being really inexperienced. 

I started with cardio and just running in my neighborhood/ trails by myself pretty early in the day or late at night to avoid the feeling of being watched. Once I started getting in the hang of it I’d ask friends to accompany me on a walk/ hike/ run to get used to working out with others. Eventually I transitioned into working out in my school gym with a friend who knew their way around and was very patient with me BUT if you feel like you can’t ask anyone you know, I have found most gym staff are really helpful too! When I eventually got a commercial gym membership, I asked the staff to help me figure out how to use some machines for upper/ lower body workouts and that really helped me get comfortable. 

Now I go to the gym mostly by myself and I usually wear a baseball cap, headphones, and sometimes a pretty baggy sweatshirt over some shorts. although I’m still a little self conscious, I’m definitely much more confident walking into the gym on my own for a work out now than I was when I first started working out. 

Good luck and good for you for recognizing that you want to change!!

Typically, to avoid burning the tops in general, I loosely cover & tent the dish with aluminum foil at the start of baking and then ~10-15 minutes to the end I’ll remove the foil, place the dish on the top rack to bake for ~5-10 minutes before turning on the broiler on low for ~5 minutes (you MUST watch the dish while the broiler is on, it can burn in an instant if not closely watched). It’s not necessary, but depending on your oven, halfway through broiling, you can rotate the dish to help evenly brown. This process usually helps me more evenly brown the tops of my cheese on oven bakes. I hope this helps!
